guide.summary: A customer-facing public OAuth integration can read shared pages via OAuth 2.0 with each customer selecting pages in the page picker. Read content capability is the least-privilege capability; only pages a customer explicitly shares are reachable.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of Notion pages that customers explicitly share with the integration. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Customers authorize individually through OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
findings.detail: Each user visits the authorization URL, selects pages in the page picker, and the app exchanges the code at the token endpoint for an access token used on behalf of that user. Only pages the user selected are accessible.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer-facing app where each customer authorizes the integration for their own workspace.

If the user clicks `Allow access` and the rest of the auth flow is not completed, the connection will *not* have access to the pages that were selected.

findings.title: Public integration required for other customer workspaces
findings.detail: Scoped integrations limited to selected workspaces cannot be listed on the Marketplace and cannot be used by other organizations; a public integration is needed to make the app available to any workspace.

evidence.quote: ## Installation scope Choose **Or select 1 or more workspaces** when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration.
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading page titles and content
findings.detail: The Read content capability allows reading existing page content and is needed for retrieving pages and their markdown; it does not allow creating or updating pages. Missing read capability returns 403. Shared child pages are readable with the parent. Requesting only read capability is the minimal choice.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading titles and content of shared pages; no create or update.

evidence.quote: * **Read content**: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
> > When a connection receives access to a Notion page or database, it can read and write to both that resource and its children.
### Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or property, or missing access to the page, returns `404`.

findings.detail: Access applies only to pages and databases the customer selects; the page picker shows only pages the user has full access to. Pages not shared return 404.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers choose which pages to share.

steps.title: Read a shared page's title and properties
steps.detail: Retrieve the shared page with the customer's OAuth access token. The page title is not always under the literal key "title"; page property keys are user-named. Find the property whose type is "title" in the properties object and read its title[].plain_text values, joining all segments. Use filter_properties=<title property name> to limit the response. Pages not in a data source return only title. Shared pages return a title for the customer's share; unshared pages return 404.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 and the title is read from the property whose type is title, joining all text segments. Boundary check: request an ID of a page the customer did not share; it must return 404, confirming access is limited to shared pages. Do not use an endpoint that writes.

## Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or missing access returns `404`.
For a page in a data source, the property values follow that data source’s schema. For a page whose parent is another page, the only property is `title`.

fields: PAGE_ID: a page the customer explicitly shared, from the page picker or URL
ACCESS_TOKEN: the customer's OAuth access token from the token exchange response

steps.title: Read a shared page's content as markdown
steps.detail: Retrieve the page body as Notion-flavored markdown with markdown_version=v2. Read the markdown field. If truncated is true, call GET /v1/pages/{id}/markdown?markdown_version=v2 for each unknown_block_ids entry and report any 404 as inaccessible rather than retrying. Unknown tags can also come from unsupported block types.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 with markdown content; truncated and unknown_block_ids are reported explicitly; each unknown block is fetched or reported inaccessible. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing requests contain only GET calls to the markdown endpoint and no create, update, or workspace-admin calls.

evidence.quote: Set the `markdown_version` query parameter to `v2` to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. `v2` is recommended. `v1` is deprecated. It's the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions.
When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the `truncated` field is set to `true` and the `unknown_block_ids` array contains the affected block IDs.
